title: Applied ML Eval Harness & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Priya Desai
body:
Overview
--------
This playbook consolidates Applied ML evaluation artifacts and operational procedures used by Redwood Inference teams to onboard models, run prompt/benchmark suites, enforce quality guardrails, create quantization profiles, and execute regression triage. The goal is to provide a single, reproducible process from model onboarding through post-deployment monitoring and incident resolution.

Scope
-----
- Eval harness configuration and standard workflows for model onboarding and continuous regression detection.
- Prompt set creation, benchmark selection, and versioned dataset management.
- Quality guardrails (automated checks, SLOs, alert thresholds).
- Recommendations for quantization profiles and validation matrices.
- Regression detection, triage, and rollback/mitigation playbook.

Ownership & Contacts
---------------------
- Primary owner: Applied ML team (applied-ml@redwood.example.com)
- Runtime/Serving contact: serving-runtime@redwood.example.com
- SRE escalation: eng-sre-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Product owner for evals: Lina Park (lina.park@redwood.example.com)

Definitions
-----------
- Eval harness: the unified CI/CD eval system that runs prompt sets, metric collectors, and regression detectors against candidate models.
- Prompt set: a curated set of inputs representing production use cases used to evaluate model quality.
- Regression: a statistically significant drop in one or more tracked quality metrics relative to a baseline model release.
- Quantization profile: a named configuration (e.g., q4_0, q8_0, fp16) describing the numeric format and operator approximations used for inference.

Quick summary of the workflow
-----------------------------
1. Model onboarding -> 2. Baseline evaluations (prompt sets + benchmarks) -> 3. Quantization & perf profiling -> 4. Canary rollout with monitoring -> 5. Regression detection -> 6. Triage & mitigation -> 7. Postmortem and artifacts update

1) Eval Harness: Standards & Onboarding
-------------------------------------
Intro: The eval harness is the single source of truth for reproducible model assessments. Teams must register models, prompt sets, and metric definitions in the harness before running automated evaluations.

Required metadata for new model registration:
- model_name (string)
- model_version (string)
- architecture (e.g., llama2, mosaic-ml, stablelm)
- tokenizer_version
- float_precision (fp32|fp16)
- primary_owner
- baseline_reference (model_version id)

Onboarding checklist (must be completed before internal canary):
1. Create model entry in eval-harness registry.
2. Add at least two production prompt sets (see Prompt Sets section).
3. Run baseline evaluation pipeline (unit + end-to-end metrics).
4. Produce quantization profile candidates and run quantized evals.
5. Produce performance profile (latency p50/p95, throughput) on target infra.
6. Security scan & dependency sign-off.

CLI example: register model and run baseline eval
```"
# register model
rwi-eval register-model --name my-model --version v1.2 --arch llama2 --owner priya.desai@redwood.example.com
# run baseline
rwi-eval run --model my-model:v1.2 --prompt-set core-qa --metrics all --output ./artifacts/my-model-v1.2
```

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
-----------------------------
Guidelines for prompt sets:
- Each prompt set should be small (200–2,000 examples) and focused by intent (e.g., "search-query-rewrite", "customer-support-summaries", "code-completion-python").
- Label examples with metadata: intent, complexity, required tokens, expected output format.
- Keep an immutable canonical copy and versioned incremental updates.

Benchmark selection:
- Use a mix of quantitative benchmarks (BLEU, ROUGE, accuracy, F1) and task-specific heuristics (e.g., API call correctness, hallucination score).
- For semantic/factual tasks, include factuality checks against an external knowledge oracle where available.
- For safety-sensitive workloads, include adversarial prompts and model safety tests.

Table: minimal prompt set manifest fields
| field | description | example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| id | unique id | core-qa-v1 |
| intent | semantic intent | customer-support |
| size | number of examples | 500 |
| owner | team | applied-ml |
| metrics | required metrics | exact_match,F1,perplexity |

3) Quality Guardrails and Metrics
----------------------------------
Key metrics to compute for each eval run (examples):
- exact_match (task-specific)
- f1_score
- bleu / rouge (generation tasks)
- perplexity (where applicable)
- embedding_distance_mean (for semantic equivalence tests)
- latency_p50, latency_p95 (ms)
- cost_per_1k_tokens (dollars)
- hallucination_rate (fraction of outputs flagged)

SLOs and alert thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Regression alert: >5% relative drop in primary metric vs baseline AND p-value < 0.05
- Latency SLO: p95 < 450ms for hosted-inference small models; p95 < 1200ms for large models on dedicated clusters
- Hallucination guard: hallucination_rate < 0.02 for knowledge-critical tasks
- Embedding drift: mean embedding distance to baseline > 0.15 -> flag for review

Automated guardrails (run in CI and production):
- Block merge if primary metric drop > 3% without signal approvals.
- Deny canary promotion if latency_p95 increased by >20% vs baseline.
- Require manual review for quantized profile that increases hallucination_rate by >1% absolute.

4) Quantization Profiles: Generation & Validation
------------------------------------------------
Strategy:
- Maintain a small set of canonical profiles: fp16, q8_0, q4_0 and platform-optimized variants (e.g., q4_0_nv, q8_1_tpu).
- For each profile create a validation matrix that includes: functional correctness tests, prompt-set metrics, token-level divergence analysis, and perf/latency numbers on target hardware.

Validation matrix (example fields):
- profile_name
- hardware_target
- metric_deltas_vs_fp16 (primary_metric: -1.2%)
- latency_p95_improvement (e.g., -28%)
- memory_reduction (e.g., -45%)
- quant_pass (true/false)

Quantization acceptance rules:
1. Primary metric drop vs fp16 <= 2% relative OR accepted by product sign-off.
2. Hallucination_rate increase <= 0.5% absolute.
3. Latency/throughput improvements meet cost-savings goals (>20% cost/token).

Example quantized eval command:
``
 rwi-eval run --model my-model:v1.2 --profile q4_0 --prompt-set core-qa --metrics exact_match,f1,latency --output artifacts/q4_0
```

5) Regression Detection & Alerting
----------------------------------
Detection signals:
- CI regression tests failing on canonical prompt sets.
- Production drift alarms: decrease in primary KPI, increased error rates, user-reported quality drops.
- Automated statistical detectors running daily comparing new window (last 24h/7d) against baseline.

Alert thresholds (examples):
- CI: primary metric drop > 3% absolute -> ticket created and severity P2.
- Production: primary metric drop > 5% relative + p < 0.05 -> P1 alert to SRE + Applied ML oncall.

6) Regression Triage Playbook (step-by-step)
-------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge & Triage (first 15 minutes)
   - Owner: oncall engineer or applied-ml oncall.
   - Correlate alerts with deploys, config changes, quantization profile changes, or data schema changes.
   - Gather initial artifacts: failing examples, eval-run ids, diffs vs baseline, perf counters.
2. Rapid rollback criteria (first 30–60 minutes)
   - If production primary metric drop > 10% OR error rate doubles -> rollback to previous stable model version and notify stakeholders.
   - If degradation is partially due to increased latency causing timeouts, throttle traffic to dedicated tier.
3. Deep analysis (2–24 hours)
   - Re-run failing prompt set with previous model, current model, and quantized variants.
   - Run embedding-drift analysis and token-level diff.
   - Check for data-pipeline changes (tokenizer updates, input normalization).
   - Evaluate paging logs for upstream changes (feature flags, prompt templating).
4. Fix & validate (24–72 hours)
   - Apply fix (model rollback, prompt template patch, update quantization profile).
   - Run full eval harness with extended prompt sets and production-sampled traffic.
   - Canary the fix with a 5–10% traffic slice for 24h before full promotion.
5. Postmortem & prevention
   - Produce a short postmortem within 3 business days.
   - Update prompt sets, regression detectors, and quantization acceptance criteria as needed.

Artifacts to attach to incident ticket:
- eval-run IDs and raw outputs (JSON)
- failing prompt examples (10–50 prioritized)
- quantization profile used and any custom kernel/ops flags
- deployment manifest and image hash
- perf profiles (p50/p95, GPU memory, token throughput)

7) Runbooks & Commands (operational playbook)
--------------------------------------------
- List active model versions
``
 rwi-serving list-models --env prod
```
- Trigger evaluation for a model against a prompt set
``
 rwi-eval run --model my-model:v1.2 --prompt-set core-qa --metrics exact_match,f1,latency --queue high
```
- Compare two eval runs
``
 rwi-eval diff --base artifacts/my-model-v1.1.json --candidate artifacts/my-model-v1.2.json --metrics exact_match,f1
```
- Promote model to canary
``
 rwi-deploy promote --model my-model:v1.2 --traffic 5% --route canary
```

8) Telemetry & Dashboards
-------------------------
Metrics to ship to observability platform (examples):
- eval.primary_metric.delta (relative % vs baseline)
- eval.latency.p50, eval.latency.p95
- eval.hallucination.rate
- eval.embedding.distance.mean
- deploy.model.version, deploy.quant.profile
- user-reported_quality_incidents (counter)

Dashboard recommendations:
- Per-model landing page with: primary metric trend, prompt-set breakdown, quantization comparisons, and canary traffic SLO panels.
- Regression triage panel: list of recent CI failures, production drift alerts, and linked incident tickets.

9) Postmortem Template (minimum content)
----------------------------------------
- Summary: short description of what happened and impact.
- Timeline: key events with timestamps.
- Root cause analysis: technical root cause and contributing factors.
- Actions: immediate remediation, short-term mitigations, long-term fixes.
- Owners and deadlines: who will do what and by when.
- Artifacts: links to eval runs, logs, commit hashes, dashboards.

Appendix A: Example Eval JSON output (excerpt)
------------------------------------------------
```
{
  "run_id": "eval-2026-04-01-001",
  "model": "my-model:v1.2",
  "prompt_set": "core-qa-v3",
  "metrics": {
    "exact_match": 0.873,
    "f1": 0.912,
    "latency_p95_ms": 402,
    "hallucination_rate": 0.007
  }
}
```

Appendix B: Common failure modes & quick mitigation checklist
--------------------------------------------------------------
- Tokenizer mismatch -> pin tokenizer version in model registry; rerun baseline.
- Quantization-induced hallucinations -> fallback to higher-precision profile for affected intents.
- Distributional drift in inputs -> collect and add new prompt samples to prompt sets; retrain if needed.
- Performance regressions -> profile kernel selection, increase batch size, or change hardware tier.
